source.changes: Adapted the twelve stat blocks of issue #171 (Reef Shark, Remorhaz, Rhinoceros, Riding Horse, Roc, Roper, Rust Monster, Saber-Toothed Tiger, Sahuagin Warrior, Salamander, Satyr and Scorpion; PDF pages 319–322 and 360) into typed mechanical fields and implementation keys. Trait, action, bonus action and reaction entries keep their source rules text, rejoined across line, column and page breaks; descriptive prose outside the stat blocks is omitted. A hit printed without dice keeps explicit zero dice. The Roper's Tentacle, whose hit prints no damage, keeps an untyped attack. No playable NPC behavior is granted.

bonus_actions.name: Swallow
bonus_actions.text: Swallow. Strength Saving Throw: DC 19, one Large or smaller creature Grappled by the remorhaz (it can have up to two creatures swallowed at a time). Failure: The target is swallowed by the remorhaz, and the Grappled condition ends. A swallowed creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the remorhaz, and it takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage at the start of each of the remorhaz’s turns. If the remorhaz takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the remorhaz must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in a space within 5 feet of the remorhaz and has the Prone condition. If the remorhaz dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

actions.text: Tentacle. Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 60 ft. Hit: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of six tentacles, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the grapple ends. actions.name: Antennae
actions.text: Antennae. The rust monster targets one nonmagical metal object—armor or a weapon—worn or carried by a creature within 5 feet of itself. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, the creature with the object. Failure: The object takes a −1 penalty to the AC it offers (armor) or to its attack rolls (weapon). Armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10, and a weapon is destroyed if its penalty reaches −5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor or weapon.
